messages.author: fd248aedd6f929a2
messages.subject: return only std.all with summary()
parts: I know it is possible to return only the std.all (and omit the std.lv) when using the standardizedSolution() command using type="std.all". Is there a way to return ony the std.all when getting output from summary()?

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: return only std.all with summary()
parts:
On 03/29/2015 08:21 PM, jimgr...@gmail.com wrote:
> I know it is possible to return only the std.all (and omit the std.lv)
> when using the standardizedSolution() command using type="std.all". Is
> there a way to return ony the std.all when getting output from summary()?

No. Not in 0.5-17.

This shows the bias of lavaan that it was designed to handle models with
latent variables. But perhaps, if no latent variables are present in the
model, it would make sense not to show the std.lv column at all.

Or did you have other motivations?

Yves.

messages.author: fd248aedd6f929a2
messages.subject: Re: return only std.all with summary()
parts:
Hi Yves, just a teaching thing. When I am first introducing lavaan output to new students I am showing them path models and it would be cleaner to not distract them with latent variable issues in the output. Just a convenience thing.
By the way, I am starting a SEM training website (aimed primarily at biologists) - featuring lavaan of course (http://www.nwrc.usgs.gov/SEM/index.html).
Best,
Jim
